# WS4

> Agent-facing index for WS4. Read the linked pages before you change the project.

## Start here

- [Home](index.html): the documentation home, with the quick-navigation table.
- [Getting started](getting-started/index.html): installation, and the two walkthroughs.
- [Quickstart: the command line](getting-started/quickstart.html): compile, simulate, target, search, watch.
- [Quickstart: the Python API](getting-started/python-api.html): the same steps as library calls.
- [Your first model](getting-started/first-model.html): a complete small study, checkable by hand.
- [How WS4 is put together](getting-started/architecture.html): the layers, the data flow, and the pitfalls.

## Concepts

- [Concepts](concepts/index.html): what the model is, in the order the ideas depend on each other.
- [The model](concepts/the-model.html): fragments, blocks, strata, tracks, treatments, rotations.
- [The simulation](concepts/the-simulation.html): the annual step, curves, and operability windows.
- [The accounting](concepts/the-accounting.html): years against periods, and what period 0 is.
- [The objective](concepts/the-objective.html): targets, weights, and the three shapes of constraint.

## Task guides

- [How-to guides](howto/index.html): the task index, with the mode (CLI or API) of each guide.
- [Prepare a dataset](howto/prepare-a-dataset.html): compile a recipe, ingest a matrix, validate.
- [Write targets](howto/write-targets.html): accounts, levels, weights, shapes, periods, calibration.
- [Even flow and non-declining yield](howto/even-flow.html): shape versus level, bands, and priming.
- [Patch size-distribution targets](howto/patch-targets.html): topology, patch accounts, and the shape-aware operators.
- [Route products to mills](howto/route-products.html): the network tables, the route configuration, and route accounts.
- [Watch a run](howto/watch-a-run.html): the live target window, several accounts at once, and `--plain`.
- [Automate a study](howto/automate-a-study.html): sweeps, in-memory targets, hand-driven solvers, and scaling.
- [FAQ](howto/faq.html): short answers to the questions that come up first.

## Examples

- [Examples gallery](examples.html): runnable notebooks, rendered with their output.

## Guides

- [Guides](guides/index.html): the deep dives.
- [Troubleshooting](guides/troubleshooting.html): symptom-first fixes.
- [Limitations and boundaries](guides/limitations-and-boundaries.html): what WS4 deliberately does not do yet.

## Reference

- [Reference](reference/index.html): the contracts, layer by layer.
- [Compiled dataset](reference/compiled-dataset.html): the runtime contract, its tables, and its invariants.
- [ForestModelXML recipe](reference/forestmodelxml.html): the recipe format, the matrix builder, legacy ingestion, and the known gaps.
- [Simulator](reference/simulator.html): the annual-step engine, its schedule, and its run outputs.
- [Optimizer](reference/optimizer.html): the objective and its targets (including even flow and non-declining yield), the operator registry, the metaheuristics, and the MIP bound.
- [Spatial structure and constraints](reference/spatial.html): the block topology, patch metrics, and opening and green-up rules.
- [Roads](reference/roads.html): the network tables, shortest-path routing, and the route outputs.
- [Performance and scale](reference/performance.html): the measured figures, the incremental objective, and how to reproduce the benchmark.
- [FEMIC hydrology](reference/femic-hydrology.html): pinned response bundles, checksums, flood-risk rows, and applicability metadata.
- [API reference](api/index.html): the repository tooling's public functions, with their parameters, types, and return values. The package API is rendered on the reference pages above.
